subject: history
title: Golden Age or Hard Times? Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll weigh whether Elizabethan England was really a 'golden age' — or hard times for many.
meta_desc: GCSE History — exploration, theatre, poverty and the verdict on Elizabethan England.
final_note: You weighed exploration, theatre and Poor Laws to judge whether this was a true 'golden age'.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Francis Drake sailed around the world between 1577 and 1580.

He brought back Spanish gold and was knighted on his ship. Walter Raleigh founded Roanoke in 1585 — the first English colony in North America. It vanished mysteriously.

The Globe Theatre opened in London in 1599.

Plays by William Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe drew up to 3,000 people. The wealthy sat in galleries; 'groundlings' paid a penny to stand. Theatre was hugely popular — though Puritans hated it.

Population grew from 3 to about 4 million during the reign.

Prices doubled, wages fell. Vagabonds wandered. The 1601 Poor Law made parishes provide work for the able-bodied poor and help the sick and old. A 'golden age' — but mainly for the rich.

What was the Elizabethan Religious Settlement of 1559?
options: Elizabeth made England fully Protestant and banned Catholic worship outright.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
Slavery was abolished because cotton was no longer profitable.
A deliberate via media — a Protestant doctrine and English-language prayer book combined with some Catholic-style ceremony — designed to maximise conformity.
